scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle (see models/circle.md) that defines this Strand's effective scope. When set, ALL Strand tracks (synthesis, discussion, etc.) share that Circle's membership, history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and encryption_profile. When unset, the Strand lives in Realm-default scope. The producer signs the corresponding Event.scope_ref; the receiver verifies that the Circle belongs to this Realm and that the derived scope equals Event.scope_ref before materializing the object's immutable effective_scope. Rebinding scope_circle_id is forbidden by default (failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden). For 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion' scenarios use two Strands linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation (circle.md §7.2).

schema_refs.description: Optional authoritative schema set for profile-defined metadata.fields subtrees. Unlike Morph, a plain Strand carries no profile subtree and omits this field entirely; when present it MUST list at least one profile schema id. The container self-schema ak.schema.strand.v1 MUST NOT appear here. Every listed profile schema and its metadata.fields namespace MUST co-occur in both directions: the ref without the subtree and the subtree without the ref are both schema_violation, evaluated on the post-patch object. Writers MUST also bind the same schema id in the Event requirements.schema[] so replay validates against the write-time schema instead of the object's current schema_refs.
schema_refs.$comment: Bidirectional co-presence for concrete profiles is enforced in allOf below; see zh/models/strand-and-message.md.

agent_participation.description: Optional wrapped agent participation ceiling for this Strand: { native_agent: { reply, accept_third_party_mention, act_on_behalf } }. When omitted, inherits the enclosing Circle ceiling (or Realm-default ceiling when scope_circle_id is unset). Each bit MAY only tighten, never widen, the parent ceiling (reducer rejects a widening write with agent_participation_ceiling_widen). The legacy flat three-bit shape is invalid v1 wire. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a strand_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata when the effective metadata_encryption_floor is e2ee_required.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a ContentBlock for Strand synthesis content.

tracks.description: Active Strand tracks, keyed by an active name in track-name-registry.json. Tracks are pure section pointers (synthesis vs discussion timeline) — they do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE. The entire Strand shares a single effective scope determined by Strand.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md); there is no per-track security boundary. At most one track entry may explicitly set is_primary=true; when none does, the reducer derives the primary track by the deterministic rules in models/strand-and-message.md §4.5. The map MUST contain at least one entry; propertyNames fails closed for names outside the registry-backed TrackName enum.

state.description: Strand lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: ak.strand.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=strand_not_active); ak.strand.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else strand_not_archived); terminal state is reached only via a ak.redaction event targeting the strand (MUST come from {'active','archived'} else strand_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.strand.archive / ak.strand.restore / ak.redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

stage.description: Optional Strand business-progression stage. Orthogonal to top-level 'state' (physical lifecycle): archive does NOT change stage; stage=done does NOT auto-archive. ak.strand.create MAY omit stage; when present it must be one of the protocol-level enum values and has no protocol-level default. The only wire path that mutates stage after creation is the dedicated ak.strand.stage.set event; ak.strand.update patches on stage / stage_changed_at MUST be rejected (schema_violation, single-source). Stage transitions intentionally do NOT carry a reason / note field — the ak.strand.stage.set event log is the audit source, and human-readable explanations belong in a Message on the discussion track that references the event. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond the core reducer hard invariants (terminal state freeze, non-active reject) defined in models/common-fields.md §5.3.3. See models/strand-and-message.md §3.2 for full semantics and models/common-fields.md §5.3 for the protocol-level enum / bucket mapping.

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition. MUST NOT appear without stage. MUST be ignored when present on wire; reducer overwrites with the triggering ak.strand.stage.set event's created_at. Same-value self-transitions (stage value unchanged) MUST NOT update this field.

not.$comment: Reject discriminator field `type`, composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`; canonical content blocks use `kind`, composite children use `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes`.

body.description: Inline text body. Authoritative bound is 256 KiB UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound. Longer bodies MUST use ak.content.long_text (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4).

content_block_long_text.description: ak.content.long_text: plain text whose full normalized UTF-8 body exceeds the 256 KiB inline boundary (or, by the narrow exception in zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4, whose Event would otherwise exceed the 1 MiB envelope limit). Exactly one of the plaintext branch (blob_ref + size_bytes + media_type) and the E2EE branch (attachment) applies. v1 core Content Block: no feature gate, no server-side opt-out.

format.description: Closed set for long text. prosemirror_json is forbidden here; structured rich text needs its own Content Block.

body.description: Inline fallback. Authoritative bound is 4096 UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound.

blob_ref.description: Hash-addressed Blob ref for the full normalized UTF-8 body. UUID blob refs are forbidden here because they carry no digest commitment.

size_bytes.description: Normalized full UTF-8 body bytes. The >256 KiB rule and the narrow Event-overflow exception are normative validator rules (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4), not a schema minimum.

media_type.description: MUST match format. No parameters: charset is fixed to UTF-8 by this kind.

format.description: Closed set for long text. prosemirror_json is forbidden here; structured rich text needs its own Content Block.

body.description: Inline fallback. Authoritative bound is 4096 UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound.

attachment.description: Encrypted full-body Blob descriptor. MUST use scheme ak.blob.stream_aead.v1 with the matching _stream alg; whole-file AEAD is forbidden for long text.

blob_ref.description: Long text MUST use a hash-addressed Blob ref; the <suite>:<hex> part MUST equal attachment.ciphertext_digest and the Blob metadata content_digest.

size_bytes.description: Normalized full UTF-8 plaintext body bytes; encrypted_attachment.size_bytes is the plaintext count that segment_count = ceil(size_bytes / segment_bytes) is derived from (zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md section 3.1 / 3.3.1). The >256 KiB rule and the narrow Event-overflow exception are normative validator rules, not a schema minimum.

strand_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Strand metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

metadata_fields.description: Profile-defined Strand metadata fields. Reducer-owned fields are forbidden here to avoid dual sources of truth.

calendar.description: Calendar event schedule subtree activated by ak.schema.calendar_event.v1 in Strand.schema_refs. See zh/models/calendar-event.md.

track_name.description: Closed active TrackName set mirrored from registry/track-name-registry.json. The artifact gate requires exact set equality; an unregistered map key is a schema violation.

strand_track.description: Strand track entry — a pure section pointer (synthesis vs discussion timeline). The track's stable name is the map key in Strand.tracks; this object holds the track's per-entry config. Tracks do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE. The whole Strand has a single effective scope determined by Strand.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md); there is no per-track security boundary. To represent 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion', create two Strands linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation per models/circle.md §7.2.

enabled.description: Whether this track currently accepts new writes (synthesis edits / discussion messages). Default true when omitted. Setting enabled=false MUST cause the reducer to reject subsequent writes to this track with 'track_disabled' until enabled is set back to true. Disabling a track does NOT delete prior history; it freezes new writes only. UI MAY hide a disabled track or render it read-only.

metadata.description: Track-local UI metadata only. The reducer NEVER interprets its keys; it does not create membership, history visibility, access, or E2EE scope. Access-like keys are rejected at the wire layer to prevent a pseudo-access surface (tracks have no independent access — see models/strand-and-message.md §4.4).

not.$comment: Forbid access-like keys so strand_track.metadata cannot smuggle a pseudo-access surface; track access is always derived from the Strand effective scope, never from track metadata.
